justification: Contributes five context-reshaping operators (Skip/Compress/Rollback/Snippet/Delete) for elastic context orchestration; the new agent is tested only on BrowseComp-style search benchmarks in the lab.
Contribution is an RL-trained ContextCurator that prunes the working memory a frozen executor reads; a novel technique measured on WebArena and DeepSearch in the lab, not in deployment.
Contribution is a dependency-graph memory that selects which past steps later actions read; new framework scored on SWE-Bench Verified/Lite against a sliding-window baseline.
Headline is a diagnosis: it names and measures premature termination as a context-rot indicator across four models and three benchmarks, a lab study of existing context-management methods.
Audits one named mechanism, context compaction, showing it silently drops governance constraints, and pins them as the fix; evidence is 1,323 lab episodes varying full-context vs compacted.
Contribution is a context-management harness keeping a complete structured interaction log searched programmatically; the new harness is scored on the ARC-AGI-3 public game set in the lab.
Contribution is an explicit situation state held outside the dialogue history rather than inferred from it; the training-free framework is tested on three interactive benchmarks across eight LLMs.

Contribution is learning reusable priors over agent collaboration topologies, the arrangement itself; a new framework evaluated on multi-domain reasoning benchmarks against topology-evolution backbones.
Contribution is a centralized orchestrator that dynamically sequences and prioritizes agents; the RL-trained paradigm is tested on closed- and open-domain benchmark scenarios, not in practice.
Contribution is an orchestration-level reward model scoring how well agents were coordinated; the self-supervised technique is measured on math, web-QA and multi-hop benchmarks in the lab.
Studies the propose-and-vote orchestration protocol itself, ablating whether agents see authorship and ongoing votes; evidence is four LLMs on GPQA-Diamond, IFEval and MuSR in the lab.
Contribution is joint adaptation of agent participation structure and orchestration policy; the new framework is benchmarked against adaptive multi-agent baselines in the lab.
Contribution is a detector that flags hallucinated or erroneous nodes and edges in agent collaboration, a check rather than an arrangement; the novel method is validated in lab experiments only.
Contribution is an orchestrator emitting role, capacity and dependency structure for the agent team; the counterfactual-RL method is scored on six reasoning and coding benchmarks in the lab.
Headline artefact is an analysis instrument: an entropy-dynamics model plus a checkpoint-dense benchmark generator used to diagnose orchestrator collapse, fitted to lab trajectories.
Contribution is semantic-entropy confidence used to verify intermediate outputs and trigger reprompting, a judgement mechanism not a topology; validated on StrategyQA, JailbreakBench and TruthfulQA.
Contribution is a routing algorithm that picks among four agent topologies per task; the proposed framework is validated on SWE-bench, GPQA and RAG tasks against static-topology baselines.
Headline artefact is a scalable benchmark plus reference scaffold and evaluation protocol for deliberative collaboration, used to evaluate representative LLMs in the lab.
Contribution is a learned meta-policy over Persist/Refine/Concede governing how agents interact, replacing fixed collaboration protocols; validated on five benchmarks against six baselines.

Contribution targets latency spend: critical-path-aware credit assignment plus a controller that eliminates redundant future agent steps, leaving the orchestration backbone intact; four lab benchmarks.
Contribution builds the arrangement per query, an operator allocator plus cost-aware LLM router driven by predicted difficulty; the new framework is tested on six benchmarks in the lab.
Contribution is a role arrangement, author-reviewers-meta-reviewer, replacing round-table debate to avoid reviewer-to-reviewer traffic; compared with MAD across benchmarks in the lab.
Contribution allocates loop spend against runtime cost signals, queue depth, cache pressure, latency and remaining budget, to meet SLOs; the RL framework is measured on five benchmarks under load.
Contribution is a structural causal action model that scores and reweights candidate next actions, an action-selection mechanism; validated on Overcooked-AI across five tasks and four LLMs.
The object is the agent arrangement itself, visible leader vs invisible orchestrator vs flat, in a preregistered 3x2 lab experiment of 365 runs rather than a deployed setting.
